clinician.trajectory_summary: A 60-year-old male presented with progressive nasal obstruction, anosmia, epistaxis, behavioral changes, and left visual loss over one year. Brain MRI and CT demonstrated a left ethmoid and sphenoid sinus mass compressing the optic apparatus. Biopsy revealed irregular glandular tissue of columnar cells with apical mucinous cytoplasm in a desmoplastic stroma, consistent with mucinous adenocarcinoma morphology. The patient underwent bicoronal craniotomy and complete tumor excision with clinical improvement. Postoperative MRI confirmed gross total resection. Although the reports lack detailed immunohistochemistry, the morphological features and clinical-imaging correlation support the diagnosis of intestinal mucinous type adenocarcinoma of the sinonasal region.
